logic_node.action: initiate_four_class_GDMT_including_SGLT2i
logic_node.action_detail: Guideline-directed medical therapy for heart failure with reduced ejection fraction now includes 4 medication classes that include sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: consider_SGLT2i_class_2a
logic_node.action_detail: SGLT2i have a Class of Recommendation 2a in HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction

concepts.name: heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: consider_SGLT2i_class_2a
logic_node.action_detail: New recommendations for HFpEF are made for SGLT2i (Class of Recommendation 2a)

concepts.name: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: continue_HFrEF_treatment
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with previous HFrEF who now have an LVEF >40% should continue their HFrEF treatment

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: assess_increased_filling_pressures
logic_node.action_detail: Evidence supporting increased filling pressures is important for the diagnosis of HF if the LVEF is >40%

logic_node.action: refer_to_HF_specialty_team
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with advanced HF who wish to prolong survival should be referred to a team specializing in HF

logic_node.action: classify_as_HFrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Classify patient as having heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)

logic_node.action: classify_as_HFpEF
logic_node.action_detail: Classify patient as having heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

logic_node.action: classify_as_HFmrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with ejection fraction of 41% to 49% should be classified as heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF)

logic_node.action: serial_EF_monitoring
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HFmrEF, one EF measurement at one time point may not be adequate, and the trajectory of LVEF over time should be evaluated

logic_node.action: Classify as Stage B: Pre-HF
logic_node.action_detail: Patients without symptoms or signs of HF but with structural heart disease (reduced systolic function, hypertrophy, chamber enlargement, wall motion abnormalities, valvular disease), elevated filling pressures, or elevated BNP/troponin should be classified as Stage B (Pre-HF).

logic_node.action: Classify as Stage C: Symptomatic HF
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with structural heart disease and current or previous symptoms of HF should be classified as Stage C.

logic_node.action: Classify as Stage D: Advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with marked HF symptoms that interfere with daily life and recurrent hospitalizations despite attempts to optimize GDMT should be classified as Stage D (Advanced HF).

logic_node.action: Classify as HFrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is defined as LVEF <= 40%.

logic_node.action: Classify as HFimpEF
logic_node.action_detail: Heart failure with improved ejection fraction (HFimpEF) is defined as previous LVEF <= 40% and a follow-up LVEF > 40%.

logic_node.action: Classify as HFmrEF
logic_node.action_detail: Heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction (HFmrEF) is defined as LVEF 41-49% with evidence of spontaneous or provokable increased LV filling pressures.

logic_node.action: Classify as HFpEF
logic_node.action_detail: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is defined as LVEF >= 50% with evidence of spontaneous or provokable increased LV filling pressures.

logic_node.action: Supports diagnosis of HFmrEF or HFpEF
logic_node.action_detail: An E/e' ratio >= 15 on Doppler echocardiography provides evidence of elevated LV filling pressures, supporting the diagnosis of HFmrEF or HFpEF.

logic_node.action: High likelihood of HFpEF diagnosis
logic_node.action_detail: H2FPEF score >= 6 (range 0-9) reflects high likelihood of HFpEF. Scores < 2 reflect low likelihood. Scores 2-5 may require further hemodynamic evaluation.

logic_node.action: Low likelihood of HFpEF
logic_node.action_detail: H2FPEF score < 2 reflects low likelihood of HFpEF. Further evaluation for alternative diagnoses should be considered.

logic_node.action: Assess vital signs and clinical congestion at each encounter
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, vital signs and evidence of clinical congestion should be assessed at each encounter to guide overall management, including adjustment of diuretics and other medications.

logic_node.action: Assess for advanced HF indicators via history and physical
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HF, clinical factors indicating the presence of advanced HF should be sought via the history and physical examination.

logic_node.action: Obtain 3-generation family history
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiomyopathy, a 3-generation family history should be obtained or updated when assessing the cause of the cardiomyopathy to identify possible inherited disease.

logic_node.action: Perform initial laboratory evaluation
logic_node.action_detail: For patients diagnosed with HF, laboratory evaluation should include CBC, urinalysis, serum electrolytes, BUN, serum creatinine, glucose, lipid profile, liver function tests, iron studies, and thyroid-stimulating hormone.

logic_node.action: Perform 12-lead ECG at initial encounter
logic_node.action_detail: For all patients presenting with HF, a 12-lead ECG should be performed at the initial encounter to optimize management.

logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP to support or exclude HF diagnosis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients presenting with dyspnea, measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP is useful to support a diagnosis or exclusion of HF.

logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP for risk stratification
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic HF, measurements of BNP or NT-proBNP levels are recommended for risk stratification.

logic_node.action: Measure BNP or NT-proBNP at admission for prognosis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized for HF, measurement of BNP or NT-proBNP levels at admission is recommended to establish prognosis.

logic_node.action: Recommend genetic screening and counseling
logic_node.action_detail: In first-degree relatives of selected patients with genetic or inherited cardiomyopathies, genetic screening and counseling are recommended to detect cardiac disease and prompt consideration of treatments to decrease HF progression and sudden death.

logic_node.action: Consider referral for genetic counseling and testing
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with nonischemic cardiomyopathy, referral for genetic counseling and testing is reasonable to identify conditions that could guide treatment for patients and family members.

logic_node.action: Perform chest x-ray
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with suspected or new-onset HF, or those presenting with acute decompensated HF, a chest x-ray should be performed to assess heart size and pulmonary congestion and to detect alternative causes of symptoms.

logic_node.action: Perform transthoracic echocardiography (TTE)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with suspected or newly diagnosed HF, TTE should be performed during initial evaluation to assess cardiac structure and function.

logic_node.action: Do not perform routine repeat assessment of LV function
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF in the absence of clinical status change, treatment interventions that might have significantly affected cardiac function, or candidacy for invasive procedures or device therapy, routine repeat assessment of LV function is not indicated.

logic_node.action: Repeat measurement of EF, structural remodeling, and valvular function
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF who have had a significant clinical change, or who have received GDMT and are being considered for invasive procedures or device therapy, repeat measurement of EF, degree of structural remodeling, and valvular function are useful.

logic_node.action: Reevaluate EF for ICD/CRT candidacy
logic_node.action_detail: Reevaluation of EF > 40 days after MI, > 90 days after revascularization, or > 90 days after GDMT initiation is useful to determine candidacy for ICD or CRT.

logic_node.action: Consider endomyocardial biopsy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, endomyocardial biopsy may be useful when a specific diagnosis is suspected that would influence therapy (e.g., amyloidosis, myocarditis).

logic_node.action: Do not perform routine invasive hemodynamic monitoring
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, routine use of invasive hemodynamic monitoring is not recommended. Routine endomyocardial biopsy should not be performed because of the risk of complications.

logic_node.action: Consider wireless PA pressure monitoring (CardioMEMS)
logic_node.action_detail: In selected adult patients with NYHA class III HF and history of HF hospitalization in the past year, on maximally tolerated stable doses of GDMT with optimal device therapy, the usefulness of wireless monitoring of PA pressure by an implanted hemodynamic monitor to reduce subsequent HF hospitalizations is uncertain (Class 2b).

logic_node.action: Assess and document NYHA functional classification
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, assessment and documentation of NYHA functional classification are recommended to determine eligibility for treatments.

logic_node.action: Perform CPET to assess candidacy for LVAD or heart transplant
logic_node.action_detail: In selected ambulatory patients with HF, cardiopulmonary exercise testing (CPET) is recommended to determine appropriateness of advanced treatments such as LVAD or heart transplant.

logic_node.action: Consider listing for heart transplantation
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with peak VO2 < 14 mL/kg/min on CPET should be considered for heart transplant listing. Those with peak VO2 >= 14 mL/kg/min can be safely followed with medical therapy.

logic_node.action: Indicates NYHA class III-IV and worse prognosis
logic_node.action_detail: A 6-minute walk distance < 300 m roughly correlates to NYHA class III to IV symptoms and is associated with worse 3-year survival free of heart transplant (62% vs 82% for >= 300 m).

logic_node.action: Use validated multivariable risk scores to estimate mortality risk
logic_node.action_detail: In ambulatory or hospitalized patients with HF, validated multivariable risk scores can be useful to estimate subsequent risk of mortality.

logic_node.action: Control blood pressure per GDMT to prevent symptomatic HF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with hypertension, blood pressure should be controlled in accordance with GDMT for hypertension to prevent symptomatic HF.

logic_node.action: Prescribe SGLT2 inhibitor to prevent HF hospitalization
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with type 2 diabetes and either established CVD or at high cardiovascular risk, SGLT2i should be used to prevent hospitalizations for HF.

logic_node.action: Target BP < 130/80 mmHg
logic_node.action_detail: A treatment goal of < 130/80 mmHg is recommended for those with a CVD risk of >= 10% to prevent HF.

logic_node.action: Target SBP < 120 mmHg for HF prevention
logic_node.action_detail: In the SPRINT trial, control to an SBP goal < 120 mmHg decreased incident HF by 38% and mortality by 23% compared with an SBP goal of < 140 mmHg. Blood pressure control is associated with approximately 40% reduction in HF events.

logic_node.action: Perform echocardiography and refer to cardiovascular specialist
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk for HF with BNP >= 50 pg/mL, screening with echocardiography and referral to a cardiovascular specialist can reduce combined rates of LV systolic dysfunction, diastolic dysfunction, and HF (STOP-HF trial).

logic_node.action: Prescribe ACE inhibitor
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with LVEF <= 40% (Stage B, pre-HF), ACEi should be used to prevent symptomatic HF and reduce mortality. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe beta blocker
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with LVEF <= 40% (Stage B), beta blockers should be used to prevent symptomatic HF. Class I, LOE B.

logic_node.action: Do not use thiazolidinediones
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with LVEF < 50%, thiazolidinediones should not be used because they increase the risk of HF, including hospitalizations. Class III: Harm, LOE B-R.

logic_node.action: Avoid nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with LVEF < 50%, nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil) with negative inotropic effects may be harmful. Class III: Harm, LOE C-LD.

logic_node.action: Prescribe statin
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with a recent or remote history of MI or ACS, statins should be used to prevent symptomatic HF and adverse cardiovascular events. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ARB as alternative to ACEi
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with a recent MI and LVEF <= 40% who are intolerant to ACEi, ARB should be used to prevent symptomatic HF and reduce mortality. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe evidence-based beta blocker to reduce mortality
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with a recent or remote history of MI or ACS and LVEF <= 40%, evidence-based beta blockers should be used to reduce mortality. Class I, LOE B.

logic_node.action: Implant ICD for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at least 40 days post-MI with LVEF <= 30% and NYHA class I symptoms on GDMT with reasonable expectation of meaningful survival > 1 year, an ICD is recommended for primary prevention of SCD to reduce total mortality. Class I, LOE B.

logic_node.action: Provide multidisciplinary team care
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HF should receive care from multidisciplinary teams to facilitate the implementation of GDMT, address potential barriers to self-care, reduce the risk of subsequent rehospitalization for HF, and improve survival. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Vaccinate against respiratory illnesses
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, vaccinating against respiratory illnesses (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID-19) is reasonable to reduce mortality. Class 2a, LOE B-NR.

logic_node.action: Initiate Step 1 GDMT: ARNi (or ACEi/ARB), beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT2i
logic_node.action_detail: For HFrEF Stage C, Step 1 medications (ARNi or ACEi/ARB, evidence-based beta blocker, MRA, and SGLT2i) may be started simultaneously at initial low doses or sequentially, guided by clinical factors, without need to achieve target dosing before initiating next medication. Doses should be increased to target as tolerated.

logic_node.action: Avoid excessive sodium intake
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with stage C HF, avoiding excessive sodium intake is reasonable to reduce congestive symptoms. Class 2a, LOE C-LD.

logic_node.action: Consider sodium intake < 2300 mg/day for general cardiovascular health
logic_node.action_detail: The AHA recommends a reduction of sodium intake to < 2300 mg/d for general cardiovascular health promotion; however, there are no trials to support this level of restriction specifically in patients with HF.

logic_node.action: Recommend exercise training or regular physical activity
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF who are able to participate, exercise training or regular physical activity is recommended to improve functional status, exercise performance, and quality of life. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe diuretics for decongestion
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF who have fluid retention, diuretics are recommended to relieve congestion, improve symptoms, and prevent worsening HF. Class I, LOE B.

logic_node.action: Add thiazide diuretic (e.g., metolazone) to loop diuretic
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF and congestive symptoms, addition of a thiazide (e.g., metolazone) to treatment with a loop diuretic should be reserved for patients who do not respond to moderate- or high-dose loop diuretics to minimize electrolyte abnormalities. Class I, LOE B.

logic_node.action: Bumetanide: start 0.5-1.0 mg once or twice daily, max 10 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Bumetanide: Initial daily dose 0.5-1.0 mg once or twice daily, maximum total daily dose 10 mg, duration of action 4-6 hours.

logic_node.action: Furosemide: start 20-40 mg once or twice daily, max 600 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Furosemide: Initial daily dose 20-40 mg once or twice daily, maximum total daily dose 600 mg, duration of action 6-8 hours.

logic_node.action: Torsemide: start 10-20 mg once daily, max 200 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Torsemide: Initial daily dose 10-20 mg once daily, maximum total daily dose 200 mg, duration of action 12-16 hours.

logic_node.action: Metolazone: start 2.5 mg once daily, max 20 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Metolazone: Initial daily dose 2.5 mg once daily, maximum total daily dose 20 mg, duration of action 12-24 hours. Used as add-on to loop diuretics for diuretic resistance.

logic_node.action: Chlorthalidone: start 12.5-25 mg once daily, max 100 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Chlorthalidone: Initial daily dose 12.5-25 mg once daily, maximum total daily dose 100 mg, duration of action 24-72 hours.

logic_node.action: Hydrochlorothiazide: start 25 mg once or twice daily, max 200 mg/day
logic_node.action_detail: Hydrochlorothiazide: Initial daily dose 25 mg once or twice daily, maximum total daily dose 200 mg, duration of action 6-12 hours.

logic_node.action: Titrate loop diuretic to achieve 0.5-1.0 kg daily weight loss
logic_node.action_detail: In outpatients with HF, diuretic therapy is commonly initiated with low doses, and the dose is increased until urine output increases and weight decreases, generally by 0.5 to 1.0 kg daily. Goal is to eliminate clinical evidence of fluid retention using the lowest dose possible to maintain euvolemia.

logic_node.action: NSAIDs can block effects of diuretics causing diuretic resistance
logic_node.action_detail: Patients may become unresponsive to high doses of diuretic drugs if they are taking agents that can block the effects of diuretics (e.g., NSAIDs) or have significant impairment of renal function or perfusion.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ARNi (sacubitril/valsartan)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II to III symptoms, the use of ARNi is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ACE inhibitor as alternative to ARNi
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with previous or current symptoms of chronic HFrEF, the use of ACEi is beneficial to reduce morbidity and mortality when the use of ARNi is not feasible. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Prescribe ARB
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic HFrEF who are intolerant to ACEi because of cough or angioedema and when the use of ARNi is not feasible, the use of ARB is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Switch from ACEi or ARB to ARNi
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic symptomatic HFrEF NYHA class II or III who tolerate an ACEi or ARB, they should be switched to an ARNi because of improvement in morbidity and mortality. Class I, LOE A.

logic_node.action: Wait at least 36 hours between ACEi and ARNi doses
logic_node.action_detail: If patients are switched from an ACEi to an ARNi or vice versa, there should be at least 36 hours between ACEi and ARNi doses to reduce the risk of angioedema.

logic_node.action: Initiate sacubitril-valsartan (ARNi) as preferred over ACEi
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF, ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan) is recommended over ACEi. PARADIGM-HF showed 20% reduction in composite of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization vs enalapril.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Initiate ARNi de novo before discharge
logic_node.action_detail: ARNi should be initiated de novo in patients hospitalized with acute HFrEF before discharge in the absence of contraindications. PIONEER-HF and TRANSITION trials support this approach.

logic_node.action: Initiate ACEi, start at low dose and titrate upward
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi reduce morbidity and mortality in HFrEF. Start at low doses and titrate to doses shown to reduce cardiovascular events. For patients for whom ARNi is inappropriate, ACEi remains strongly advised.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Use ACEi with caution
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi should be given with caution to patients with elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L), low systemic blood pressure, or renal insufficiency.

logic_node.action: Initiate ARB as alternative to ACEi
logic_node.action_detail: Patients intolerant to ACEi because of cough or angioedema should be started on ARB. Start at low doses and titrate upward. ARB should be given with caution with potassium >5.0 mEq/L.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Use ARB with caution
logic_node.action_detail: ARB should be given with caution to patients with low systemic blood pressure, renal insufficiency, or elevated serum potassium (>5.0 mEq/L).

logic_node.action: Switch from ACEi/ARB to ARNi (sacubitril-valsartan)
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with chronic stable HFrEF who tolerate ACEi or ARB should be switched to ARNi. Target dose: sacubitril-valsartan 200 mg twice daily (ARB component equivalent to valsartan 160 mg).

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Do not administer ARNi
logic_node.action_detail: ARNi therapy should not be administered in patients with a history of angioedema because of increased risk of recurrence.

logic_node.action: Do not administer ARNi concomitantly with ACEi; 36-hour washout required
logic_node.action_detail: Concomitant use of neprilysin inhibitors with ACEi is contraindicated due to risk of angioedema. ARNi should not be administered within 36 hours of switching from or to an ACEi.

logic_node.action: Do not administer ACEi
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi should not be administered to patients with any history of angioedema. ARB may be used with caution as alternative.

logic_node.action: Prescribe one of 3 evidence-based beta blockers: bisoprolol, carvedilol, or sustained-release metoprolol succinate
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF with current or previous symptoms, use of 1 of the 3 beta blockers proven to reduce mortality (bisoprolol, carvedilol, sustained-release metoprolol succinate) is recommended to reduce mortality and hospitalizations. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Initiate beta blocker at low dose, titrate to target dose
logic_node.action_detail: Beta blockers should be initiated at low doses and every effort should be made to achieve target doses of the beta blockers shown to be effective in major clinical trials, as tolerated. Even if symptoms do not improve, long-term treatment should be maintained.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Initiate beta blocker before hospital discharge
logic_node.action_detail: Beta blockers can be safely initiated before hospital discharge, provided patients are clinically stabilized and do not require intravenous inotropic therapy for HF. Only bisoprolol, carvedilol, and sustained-release metoprolol succinate are recommended; this is not a class effect.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Initiate MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and NYHA class II-IV symptoms, an MRA (spironolactone or eplerenone) is recommended to reduce morbidity and mortality, if eGFR >30 mL/min/1.73m2 and serum potassium <5.0 mEq/L. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Discontinue MRA
logic_node.action_detail: In patients taking MRA whose serum potassium cannot be maintained at <5.5 mEq/L, MRA should be discontinued to avoid life-threatening hyperkalemia. COR 3 (Harm), LOE B-NR.

logic_node.action: Monitor potassium and renal function at initiation and closely thereafter
logic_node.action_detail: Careful monitoring of potassium, renal function, and diuretic dosing should be performed at initiation and closely monitored thereafter to minimize risk of hyperkalemia and renal insufficiency.

logic_node.action: Do not initiate MRA
logic_node.action_detail: eGFR <=30 mL/min/1.73m2 is a contraindication to MRA initiation.

logic_node.action: Do not initiate MRA
logic_node.action_detail: Serum potassium >=5.0 mEq/L is a contraindication to MRA initiation.

logic_node.action: Spironolactone/eplerenone 25 mg daily, increase to 50 mg daily after 1 month
logic_node.action_detail: Starting dose of spironolactone and eplerenone is 25 mg orally daily, increased to 50 mg daily orally after a month.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Reduce MRA dose by half (spironolactone/eplerenone 12.5 mg daily)
logic_node.action_detail: For eGFR 31-49 mL/min/1.73m2, MRA dosing should be reduced by half.

logic_node.action: Check potassium at 1 week, 4 weeks, then every 6 months
logic_node.action_detail: Regular checks of serum potassium levels and renal function should be performed approximately 1 week, then 4 weeks, then every 6 months after initiating or intensifying MRA, with more frequent testing for clinical instability.

logic_node.action: Prescribe SGLT2i (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic chronic HFrEF, SGLT2i are recommended to reduce hospitalization for HF and cardiovascular mortality, irrespective of the presence of type 2 diabetes. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Avoid SGLT2i (excluded from trials)
logic_node.action_detail: SGLT2i trials excluded patients with eGFR <20 mL/min/1.73m2 (EMPEROR-Reduced) or <30 mL/min/1.73m2 (DAPA-HF). Type 1 diabetes and SBP <95-100 mmHg were also exclusions.

logic_node.action: Add hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate combination
logic_node.action_detail: For self-identified African American patients with NYHA class III-IV HFrEF on optimal medical therapy, hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate is recommended to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity and mortality. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate combination
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF who cannot take ARNi, ACEi, or ARB because of drug intolerance or renal insufficiency, hydralazine and isosorbide dinitrate might be considered. COR IIb, LOE C-LD.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider omega-3 PUFA supplementation as adjunctive therapy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF class II-IV symptoms, omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid supplementation may be reasonable as adjunctive therapy to reduce mortality and cardiovascular hospitalizations. COR IIb, LOE B-R.

logic_node.action: Do not use anticoagulation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic HFrEF without a specific indication (VTE, AF, previous thromboembolic event, or cardioembolic source), anticoagulation is not recommended. COR 3 (No Benefit), LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Do not use dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers for HF treatment
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, dihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended treatment for HF. COR 3 (No Benefit), LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Avoid nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers (diltiazem, verapamil)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, nondihydropyridine calcium channel-blocking drugs are not recommended. COR 3 (Harm), LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Avoid class IC antiarrhythmics and dronedarone
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, class IC antiarrhythmic medications and dronedarone may increase the risk of mortality. COR 3 (Harm), LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Avoid thiazolidinediones
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, thiazolidinediones increase the risk of worsening HF symptoms and hospitalizations. COR 3 (Harm), LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Avoid saxagliptin and alogliptin (DPP-4 inhibitors)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with type 2 diabetes and high cardiovascular risk, DPP-4 inhibitors saxagliptin and alogliptin increase the risk of HF hospitalization and should be avoided in patients with HF. COR 3 (Harm), LOE B-R.

logic_node.action: Avoid NSAIDs
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, NSAIDs worsen HF symptoms and should be avoided or withdrawn whenever possible. COR 3 (Harm), LOE B-NR.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Initiate all 4 pillars of GDMT simultaneously or in rapid sequence
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, simultaneous or rapid-sequence initiation of the 4 foundational therapies (ARNi/ACEi/ARB, beta blocker, MRA, SGLT2i) is recommended rather than sequential addition and uptitration of one drug at a time.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Prescribe ivabradine to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF (LVEF <=35%) in sinus rhythm with resting heart rate >=70 bpm on maximally tolerated beta blocker, ivabradine can be beneficial. COR IIa, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider digoxin to decrease HF hospitalizations
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with symptomatic HFrEF despite GDMT (or unable to tolerate GDMT), digoxin might be considered to decrease hospitalizations for HF. COR IIb, LOE B-R. Keep serum digoxin level 0.5-0.9 ng/mL.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Monitor serum digoxin level, target 0.5-0.9 ng/mL
logic_node.action_detail: Use of digoxin requires caution. Serum digoxin concentration should be maintained between 0.5-0.9 ng/mL. Higher levels associated with increased mortality.

logic_node.action: Consider vericiguat to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death
logic_node.action_detail: In select high-risk patients with HFrEF and recent worsening HF already on GDMT, oral soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator (vericiguat) may be considered to reduce HF hospitalization and cardiovascular death. COR IIb, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Implant ICD for primary prevention of sudden cardiac death
logic_node.action_detail: ICD therapy is recommended for primary prevention of SCD in patients with symptomatic HFrEF (LVEF <=35%) despite >=3 months of GDMT, who have reasonable expectation of meaningful survival for >1 year. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Implant CRT (or CRT-D) to reduce morbidity and mortality
logic_node.action_detail: CRT is indicated for patients who have LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with QRS duration >=150 ms, and NYHA class II-III or ambulatory class IV symptoms on GDMT. COR I, LOE A.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: CRT can be useful (LBBB, QRS 120-149 ms)
logic_node.action_detail: CRT can be useful in patients with LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, LBBB with QRS 120-149 ms, NYHA class II-III or ambulatory IV on GDMT. COR IIa, LOE B.

logic_node.action: CRT may be considered (non-LBBB, QRS >=150 ms, NYHA III-IV)
logic_node.action_detail: CRT may be considered in patients with LVEF <=35%, sinus rhythm, non-LBBB with QRS >=150 ms, NYHA class III or ambulatory IV on GDMT. COR IIb, LOE B.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: CRT is not indicated
logic_node.action_detail: CRT is not recommended in patients with QRS duration <120 ms. COR 3 (No Benefit).

logic_node.action: Consider cardiac contractility modulation (CCM)
logic_node.action_detail: CCM is FDA-approved for patients with NYHA class III, LVEF 25-45% who are not candidates for CRT. RCTs show benefits in exercise capacity and QOL but no mortality benefit yet.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Surgical revascularization (CABG) plus GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HF, reduced EF (<=35%), and suitable coronary anatomy, surgical revascularization plus GDMT is beneficial to improve symptoms, cardiovascular hospitalizations, and long-term all-cause mortality. COR I, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Optimize GDMT before considering intervention for secondary MR
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with chronic severe secondary MR and HFrEF, optimization of GDMT is recommended before any intervention for secondary MR related to LV dysfunction. COR I, LOE C-LD.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER)
logic_node.action_detail: Transcatheter edge-to-edge MV repair (TEER) is beneficial in patients with persistent symptoms despite GDMT, appropriate anatomy, LVEF 20-50%, LVESD <=70 mm, and PA systolic pressure <=70 mmHg. Based on COAPT trial.

concepts.name: heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Prescribe SGLT2i for HFmrEF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFmrEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality. COR IIa, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider HFrEF GDMT (beta blocker, ARNi/ACEi/ARB, MRA)
logic_node.action_detail: Among patients with symptomatic HFmrEF (LVEF 41-49%), use of evidence-based beta blockers, ARNi, ACEi/ARB, and MRAs may be considered, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum. COR IIb, LOE B-NR.

concepts.name: heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Continue GDMT to prevent relapse
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFimpEF after treatment, GDMT should be continued to prevent relapse of HF and LV dysfunction, even in patients who may become asymptomatic. COR I, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with improved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Titrate antihypertensives to blood pressure targets
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HFpEF and hypertension should have medication titrated to attain blood pressure targets in accordance with published clinical practice guidelines to prevent morbidity. COR I, LOE C-LD.

concepts.name: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Prescribe SGLT2i for HFpEF
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFpEF, SGLT2i can be beneficial in decreasing HF hospitalizations and cardiovascular mortality. COR IIa, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Consider MRA to decrease hospitalizations in selected patients
logic_node.action_detail: In selected patients with HFpEF, MRAs may be considered to decrease hospitalizations, particularly among patients with LVEF on the lower end of this spectrum. COR IIb, LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Do not routinely use nitrates or PDE-5 inhibitors
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFpEF, routine use of nitrates or phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors to increase activity or QOL is ineffective. COR 3 (No Benefit), LOE B-R.

concepts.name: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

logic_node.action: Screen for monoclonal light chains (serum/urine IFE and serum free light chains)
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis (LV wall thickness >=14 mm with fatigue, dyspnea, or edema, especially with ECG-echo discordance) should have screening with serum and urine immunofixation electrophoresis and serum free light chains. COR I, LOE B-NR.

logic_node.action: Perform bone scintigraphy (99mTc-PYP scan)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with high clinical suspicion for cardiac amyloidosis without evidence of monoclonal light chains, bone scintigraphy should be performed to confirm transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. COR I, LOE B-NR.

logic_node.action: Perform TTR gene sequencing
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, genetic testing with TTR gene sequencing is recommended to differentiate hereditary variant from wild-type. COR I, LOE B-NR.

logic_node.action: Diagnose ATTR-CM (noninvasive)
logic_node.action_detail: Grade 2/3 cardiac uptake on 99mTc-PYP scan (or H/CL ratio >1.5) in the absence of monoclonal protein has very high specificity and positive predictive value for ATTR-CM. SPECT should confirm myocardial retention.

logic_node.action: Prescribe tafamidis (TTR stabilizer)
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with wild-type or variant transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and NYHA class I-III symptoms, tafamidis is indicated to reduce cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. COR I, LOE B-R.

logic_node.action: Anticoagulate regardless of CHA2DS2-VASc score
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiac amyloidosis and AF, anticoagulation is reasonable to reduce the risk of stroke regardless of the CHA2DS2-VASc score. COR IIa, LOE C-LD.

logic_node.action: Use GDMT with caution (may be poorly tolerated)
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with ATTR-CM and EF <=40%, standard GDMT (ARNi, ACEi, ARB, beta blockers) may be poorly tolerated. Vasodilators may exacerbate hypotension with autonomic dysfunction. Beta blockers may worsen HF as patients rely on heart rate to maintain cardiac output.

logic_node.action: Tafamidis meglumine 80 mg (4x20 mg capsules) once daily OR tafamidis 61 mg once daily
logic_node.action_detail: Tafamidis meglumine is available in 20-mg capsules; FDA-approved dose is 80 mg (4 capsules) once daily. Tafamidis is also available in 61-mg capsules; FDA-approved dose is 61 mg once daily. Not beneficial in NYHA class IV, severe aortic stenosis, or eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2.

logic_node.action: Tafamidis not beneficial in NYHA class IV
logic_node.action_detail: Benefit of tafamidis has not been observed in patients with NYHA class IV symptoms, severe aortic stenosis, or eGFR <25 mL/min/1.73m2.

logic_node.action: Classify as advanced heart failure
logic_node.action_detail: All 4 ESC criteria must be present despite optimal GDMT: 1) NYHA III-IV, 2) Severe cardiac dysfunction (LVEF<=30%, isolated RV failure, nonoperable severe valve/congenital abnormalities, or EF>=40% with elevated natriuretic peptides and diastolic dysfunction), 3) HF hospitalizations in past 12mo, 4) Severe exercise impairment (6MWT<300m or peak VO2<12-14 mL/kg/min)

logic_node.action: Meets exercise impairment criterion for advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: 6-minute walk test distance <300 m estimated to be of cardiac origin meets criterion 4 for advanced HF

logic_node.action: Meets exercise impairment criterion for advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: Peak VO2 <12-14 mL/kg/min estimated to be of cardiac origin meets criterion 4 for advanced HF

logic_node.action: Refer to HF specialty care
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with advanced HF, when consistent with the patient's goals of care, timely referral for HF specialty care is recommended to review HF management and assess suitability for advanced HF therapies (LVAD, cardiac transplantation, palliative care, palliative inotropes)

logic_node.action: I-NEED-HELP criterion E: consider advanced HF referral
logic_node.action_detail: EF <= 35% is one of the I-NEED-HELP criteria for decision-making for referral to advanced HF. Other criteria: I-Intravenous inotropes, N-NYHA IIIB-IV or elevated natriuretic peptides, E-End-organ dysfunction, D-Defibrillator shocks, H-Hospitalizations>1, E-Edema despite escalating diuretics, L-Low SBP<=90/high HR, P-Progressive GDMT intolerance

logic_node.action: Fluid restriction benefit uncertain
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with advanced HF and hyponatremia, the benefit of fluid restriction to reduce congestive symptoms is uncertain

logic_node.action: Clinical indicator of advanced HF
logic_node.action_detail: Severely reduced exercise capacity (peak VO2 <14 mL/kg/min or <50% predicted, 6MWT <300m) is a clinical indicator of advanced HF triggering referral consideration

logic_node.action: Clinical indicator of advanced HF - escalating diuretics
logic_node.action_detail: Daily furosemide equivalent dose >160 mg/d or use of supplemental metolazone therapy indicates advanced HF

logic_node.action: Clinical indicator of advanced HF - frequent hypotension
logic_node.action_detail: Frequent SBP <= 90 mm Hg is a clinical indicator of advanced HF

logic_node.action: Clinical indicator of advanced HF - persistent hyponatremia
logic_node.action_detail: Persistent hyponatremia (serum sodium <134 mEq/L) is a clinical indicator of advanced HF

logic_node.action: Clinical indicator of advanced HF - high predicted mortality
logic_node.action_detail: Increased predicted 1-year mortality >20% according to HF survival models (MAGGIC, SHFM) is a clinical indicator of advanced HF

logic_node.action: Continuous IV inotropic support as bridge therapy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with stage D HF refractory to GDMT and device therapy who are eligible for and awaiting MCS or cardiac transplantation, continuous IV inotropic support is reasonable as bridge therapy

logic_node.action: Consider continuous IV inotropic support for palliation
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with stage D HF despite optimal GDMT and device therapy who are ineligible for MCS or transplantation, continuous IV inotropic support may be considered as palliative therapy

logic_node.action: Avoid long-term continuous or intermittent IV inotropes
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, long-term use of continuous or intermittent IV inotropic agents, for reasons other than palliative care or bridge to advanced therapies, is potentially harmful (Class 3: Harm)

logic_node.action: Meets indications for durable MCS consideration
logic_node.action_detail: Indications for durable MCS include: frequent HF hospitalizations, NYHA IIIb-IV despite maximal therapy, intolerance of neurohormonal antagonists, increasing diuretic requirement, symptomatic despite CRT, inotrope dependence, low peak VO2 (<14-16), end-organ dysfunction attributable to low cardiac output

logic_node.action: Relative contraindication to durable MCS destination therapy
logic_node.action_detail: Age >80 years is a relative contraindication to durable MCS for destination therapy. Absolute contraindications include irreversible hepatic/renal/neurological disease, medical nonadherence, severe psychosocial limitations.

logic_node.action: Dopamine 5-10 mcg/kg/min (inotropic) or 10-15 mcg/kg/min (vasopressor)
logic_node.action_detail: Dopamine infusion: 5-10 mcg/kg/min for inotropic effect (increases CO, HR), 10-15 mcg/kg/min for vasopressor effect (increases SVR). t1/2 2-20 min. Caution with MAO-I.

logic_node.action: Dobutamine 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min
logic_node.action_detail: Dobutamine infusion 2.5-20 mcg/kg/min. t1/2 2-3 min, hepatic metabolism. Increases CO and HR. Caution: MAO-I; CI: sulfite allergy.

logic_node.action: Milrinone 0.125-0.75 mcg/kg/min
logic_node.action_detail: Milrinone (PDE3 inhibitor) infusion 0.125-0.75 mcg/kg/min. Bolus not recommended. t1/2 2.5h. Decreases SVR and PVR. Accumulation in renal failure; monitor kidney function and LFTs.

logic_node.action: Monitor kidney function and LFTs
logic_node.action_detail: Milrinone accumulation may occur in renal failure; monitor kidney function and LFTs

logic_node.action: Norepinephrine 0.5-30 mcg/min
logic_node.action_detail: Norepinephrine infusion 0.5-30 mcg/min (not weight-based). t1/2 2.5 min. Increases SVR strongly. Caution: MAO-I. Risk of tissue necrosis.

logic_node.action: Durable LVAD implantation
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with advanced HFrEF with NYHA class IV symptoms who are deemed dependent on continuous IV inotropes or temporary MCS, durable LVAD implantation is effective to improve functional status, QOL, and survival

logic_node.action: Consider durable MCS
logic_node.action_detail: In select patients with advanced HFrEF who have NYHA class IV symptoms despite GDMT, durable MCS can be beneficial to improve symptoms, functional class, and reduce mortality

logic_node.action: Cardiac transplantation
logic_node.action_detail: For selected patients with advanced HF despite GDMT, cardiac transplantation is indicated to improve survival and QOL

logic_node.action: Assess congestion severity and perfusion adequacy
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized with HF, severity of congestion and adequacy of perfusion should be assessed to guide triage and initial therapy

logic_node.action: Address reversible factors, optimize volume, advance GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: For patients admitted with HF, treatment should address reversible factors, establish optimal volume status, and advance GDMT toward targets for outpatient therapy

logic_node.action: Continue and optimize preexisting GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF requiring hospitalization, preexisting GDMT should be continued and optimized to improve outcomes, unless contraindicated

logic_node.action: Do not routinely discontinue diuresis and GDMT
logic_node.action_detail: In patients experiencing mild decrease of renal function or asymptomatic reduction of blood pressure during HF hospitalization, diuresis and other GDMT should not routinely be discontinued

logic_node.action: Initiate GDMT during hospitalization
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, GDMT should be initiated during hospitalization after clinical stability is achieved

logic_node.action: Reinitiate and optimize GDMT as soon as possible
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF, if discontinuation of GDMT is necessary during hospitalization, it should be reinitiated and further optimized as soon as possible

logic_node.action: Prompt IV loop diuretics
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with HF admitted with evidence of significant fluid overload should be promptly treated with intravenous loop diuretics to improve symptoms and reduce morbidity

logic_node.action: Titrate diuretics to resolve congestion before discharge
logic_node.action_detail: For patients hospitalized with HF, therapy with diuretics should be titrated with a goal to resolve clinical evidence of congestion to reduce symptoms and rehospitalizations

logic_node.action: Intensify diuretic regimen: higher IV loop diuretic doses or add second diuretic
logic_node.action_detail: When diuresis is inadequate, intensify using higher doses of IV loop diuretics or add a second diuretic (sequential nephron blockade with thiazide). Titration often starts at 2x home dose administered IV.

logic_node.action: Discharge plan should include diuretic adjustment strategy
logic_node.action_detail: For patients requiring diuretic treatment during hospitalization for HF, the discharge regimen should include a plan for adjustment of diuretics to decrease rehospitalizations

logic_node.action: Consider IV nitroglycerin or nitroprusside as adjuvant to diuretics
logic_node.action_detail: In patients admitted with decompensated HF, in the absence of systemic hypotension, IV nitroglycerin or nitroprusside may be considered as adjuvant to diuretic therapy for relief of dyspnea

logic_node.action: VTE prophylaxis
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized with HF, prophylaxis for VTE is recommended to prevent venous thromboembolic disease using subcutaneous LMWH, unfractionated heparin, fondaparinux, or approved DOAC

logic_node.action: IV inotropic support to maintain perfusion
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, IV inotropic support should be used to maintain systemic perfusion and preserve end-organ performance

logic_node.action: Temporary MCS
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, temporary MCS is reasonable when end-organ function cannot be maintained by pharmacologic means

logic_node.action: Multidisciplinary shock team management
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, management by a multidisciplinary team experienced in shock is reasonable

logic_node.action: Consider PA catheter placement
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiogenic shock, PA catheter placement may be considered to define hemodynamic subsets and guide management

logic_node.action: Triage to center capable of temporary MCS
logic_node.action_detail: For patients not rapidly responding to initial shock measures, triage to centers that can provide temporary MCS may be considered

logic_node.action: Diagnose cardiogenic shock
logic_node.action_detail: Cardiogenic shock clinical criteria: SBP <90 mmHg for >30 min (or MAP <60 for >30 min, or requiring vasopressors) PLUS hypoperfusion (decreased mentation, cold extremities, urine output <30 mL/h, or lactate >2 mmol/L)

logic_node.action: Hemodynamic confirmation of cardiogenic shock
logic_node.action_detail: Hemodynamic criteria: cardiac index <2.2 L/min/m2, PCWP >15 mmHg. Additional markers: cardiac power output <0.6W, shock index (HR/SBP) >1.0. RV shock: PAPi and CVP >15 mmHg.

logic_node.action: Refer to multidisciplinary HF disease management program
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with high-risk HF, particularly those with recurrent hospitalizations for HFrEF, referral to multidisciplinary HF disease management programs is recommended to reduce the risk of hospitalization

logic_node.action: Patient-centered discharge instructions with transitional care plan
logic_node.action_detail: In patients hospitalized with worsening HF, patient-centered discharge instructions with a clear plan for transitional care should be provided before hospital discharge

logic_node.action: Early follow-up within 7 days of discharge
logic_node.action_detail: In patients discharged after hospitalization for worsening HF, an early follow-up generally within 7 days is reasonable to optimize care and reduce rehospitalization

logic_node.action: Transitional care plan elements
logic_node.action_detail: Transitional care plan should include: address precipitating causes, adjust diuretics based on volume/weight/electrolytes, coordinate safety labs after GDMT changes, plan for GDMT resumption/initiation/titration, reinforce education, address high-risk comorbidities, consider cardiac rehab referral, consider palliative care referral

logic_node.action: IV iron replacement
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and iron deficiency with or without anemia, IV iron replacement is reasonable to improve functional status and QOL

logic_node.action: Do not use erythropoietin-stimulating agents
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and anemia, erythropoietin-stimulating agents should not be used to improve morbidity and mortality (Class 3: Harm)

logic_node.action: Uptitrate GDMT to maximally tolerated target dose
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HFrEF and hypertension, uptitration of GDMT to the maximally tolerated target dose is recommended

logic_node.action: Formal sleep assessment
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and suspicion of sleep-disordered breathing, a formal sleep assessment is reasonable to confirm diagnosis and differentiate obstructive from central sleep apnea

logic_node.action: Consider CPAP
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and obstructive sleep apnea, continuous positive airway pressure may be reasonable to improve sleep quality and decrease daytime sleepiness

logic_node.action: Do not use adaptive servo-ventilation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with NYHA class II to IV HF and central sleep apnea, adaptive servo-ventilation causes harm (Class 3: Harm)

logic_node.action: SGLT2 inhibitor
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF and type 2 diabetes, SGLT2i is recommended for hyperglycemia management and to reduce HF-related morbidity and mortality

logic_node.action: Iron deficiency confirmed
logic_node.action_detail: Iron deficiency defined as ferritin <100 mcg/L. IV iron repletion shown to improve exercise capacity and QOL in HFrEF.

logic_node.action: Functional iron deficiency confirmed
logic_node.action_detail: Iron deficiency also defined as ferritin 100-300 mcg/L with transferrin saturation <20%

logic_node.action: Chronic anticoagulant therapy
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc >= 2 (men) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy

logic_node.action: Chronic anticoagulant therapy
logic_node.action_detail: Patients with chronic HF with AF and CHA2DS2-VASc >= 3 (women) should receive chronic anticoagulant therapy

logic_node.action: DOAC preferred over warfarin
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with chronic HF with AF, DOAC is recommended over warfarin in eligible patients

logic_node.action: Consider AF ablation
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF and symptoms caused by AF, AF ablation is reasonable to improve symptoms and QOL

logic_node.action: AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with AF and LVEF <= 50%, if rhythm control fails or is not desired and ventricular rates remain rapid despite medical therapy, AV nodal ablation with CRT implantation is reasonable

logic_node.action: Consider chronic anticoagulation even without additional risk factors
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with chronic HF and AF, chronic anticoagulant therapy is reasonable for men and women without additional risk factors (HF itself confers stroke risk)

logic_node.action: Multidisciplinary discussion on cancer therapy continuation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients who develop cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy or HF, a multidisciplinary discussion involving the patient about the risk-benefit ratio of cancer therapy interruption, discontinuation, or continuation is recommended

logic_node.action: Initiate ARB, ACEi, and beta blockers
logic_node.action_detail: In asymptomatic patients with cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy (EF <50%), ARB, ACEi, and beta blockers are reasonable to prevent progression to HF and improve cardiac function

logic_node.action: Pretherapy cardiac function evaluation
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with cardiovascular risk factors or known cardiac disease being considered for potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, pretherapy evaluation of cardiac function is reasonable to establish baseline

logic_node.action: Serial cardiac function monitoring
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with CV risk factors or cardiac disease receiving potentially cardiotoxic anticancer therapies, monitoring of cardiac function is reasonable for early identification of drug-induced cardiomyopathy

logic_node.action: Beta blockers and ACEi/ARB for primary prevention uncertain
logic_node.action_detail: In patients at risk of cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy, initiation of beta blockers and ACEi/ARB for the primary prevention of drug-induced cardiomyopathy is of uncertain benefit

logic_node.action: Consider serial cardiac troponin measurement
logic_node.action_detail: In patients being considered for potentially cardiotoxic therapies, serial measurement of cardiac troponin might be reasonable for further risk stratification

logic_node.action: Serial cardiac function monitoring (echocardiography)
logic_node.action_detail: Patients receiving doxorubicin or epirubicin should undergo serial cardiac function monitoring during treatment, as these agents are known to be associated with cardiomyopathy.

logic_node.action: Serial cardiac function monitoring (echocardiography)
logic_node.action_detail: Patients receiving trastuzumab or pertuzumab should undergo serial cardiac function monitoring during treatment, as these agents are known to be associated with cardiomyopathy.

logic_node.action: Enhanced cardiac monitoring during cancer therapy
logic_node.action_detail: Patients aged >= 60 years are at higher risk for cancer therapy-related cardiomyopathy and should be monitored more closely. Other risk factors include Black race, CAD, hypertension, diabetes, preexisting cardiomyopathy, previous anthracycline exposure, previous chest radiation, and elevated pre-therapy troponin.

logic_node.action: Provide patient-centered counseling regarding contraception and cardiovascular risks during pregnancy
logic_node.action_detail: In women with a history of HF or cardiomyopathy, including previous peripartum cardiomyopathy, patient-centered counseling regarding contraception and the risks of cardiovascular deterioration during pregnancy should be provided.

logic_node.action: Consider anticoagulation at diagnosis until 6-8 weeks postpartum
logic_node.action_detail: In women with acute HF caused by peripartum cardiomyopathy and LVEF <30%, anticoagulation may be reasonable at diagnosis, until 6 to 8 weeks postpartum, although the efficacy and safety are uncertain.

logic_node.action: Do NOT administer ACEi, ARB, ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, ivabradine, or vericiguat
logic_node.action_detail: In women with HF or cardiomyopathy who are pregnant or currently planning for pregnancy, ACEi, ARB, ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, ivabradine, and vericiguat should not be administered because of significant risks of fetal harm.

logic_node.action: Diagnose peripartum cardiomyopathy
logic_node.action_detail: Peripartum cardiomyopathy is defined as systolic dysfunction, typically LVEF <45%, often with LV dilation, occurring in late pregnancy or early postpartum with no other identifiable cardiomyopathy cause.

logic_node.action: Classify as high risk for subsequent pregnancy
logic_node.action_detail: LVEF <50% before a subsequent pregnancy is the strongest prognostic determinant of adverse outcomes in women with previous peripartum cardiomyopathy. An international systematic review reported 48% further LVEF deterioration, 49% HF symptoms, and 16% mortality in those with persistent LV dysfunction.

logic_node.action: Administer at least prophylactic-dosed anticoagulation with bromocriptine
logic_node.action_detail: In women with severe acute HF caused by peripartum cardiomyopathy and LVEF <35%, if bromocriptine is used, it should be accompanied by at least prophylactic-dosed anticoagulation because of the potential association with thromboembolic events.

logic_node.action: Discontinue ACEi, ARB, ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, ivabradine; continue beta-blocker (metoprolol preferred), hydralazine, and nitrates
logic_node.action_detail: For women planning pregnancy imminently, discontinue ACEi, ARB, ARNi, MRA, SGLT2i, or ivabradine. Within a construct of multidisciplinary shared decision-making, continue beta-blocker (most commonly metoprolol), hydralazine, and nitrates. Adjust diuretic dosing to minimize placental hypoperfusion risk. Repeat echocardiography approximately 3 months after medication adjustments.

logic_node.action: Repeat echocardiography approximately 3 months after preconception HF medication adjustments
logic_node.action_detail: Ideally, repeat echocardiography approximately 3 months after preconception HF medication adjustments to ensure stability of myocardial structure and function before conception.

logic_node.action: Prefer metoprolol as beta-blocker; monitor neonatal heart rate
logic_node.action_detail: Postpartum women can use beta-blockers (metoprolol preferred, monitor neonatal heart rate). Diuretics can suppress lactation, but with neonatal follow-up furosemide may be appropriate.

logic_node.action: ACEi and ARB are strictly contraindicated
logic_node.action_detail: ACEi and ARB are associated with second- and third-trimester renal and tubular dysplasia, oligohydramnios, fetal growth restriction, ossification disorders of the skull, lung hypoplasia, contractures, large joints, anemia, and intrauterine fetal death and are strictly contraindicated.

logic_node.action: Spironolactone contraindicated due to feminization risk
logic_node.action_detail: Spironolactone has sufficient data regarding dose-dependent feminization of male offspring to raise concern and is contraindicated in pregnancy.

logic_node.action: Start ACEi (enalapril or captopril preferred) and metoprolol for breastfeeding postpartum women
logic_node.action_detail: Postpartum women who breastfeed can start ACEi (enalapril or captopril preferred), and metoprolol remains the preferred beta blocker.

logic_node.action: Routine echocardiographic screening in the third trimester
logic_node.action_detail: Consider routine echocardiographic screening in the third trimester for reassessment of myocardial structure and function before labor. Echocardiography for any significant changes in HF symptoms or signs during pregnancy. BNP or NT-proBNP monitoring during pregnancy may have some value for prediction of cardiovascular events.

logic_node.action: Provide palliative and supportive care including high-quality communication, prognosis conveyance, goal clarification, shared decision-making, symptom management, and caregiver support
logic_node.action_detail: For all patients with HF, palliative and supportive care should be provided to improve QOL and relieve suffering. (COR 1, LOE C-LD)

logic_node.action: Perform laboratory monitoring with new MRA therapy (PM-10)
logic_node.action_detail: Laboratory monitoring should be performed when initiating MRA therapy in patients with HFrEF to monitor for hyperkalemia and renal function changes.

logic_node.action: Execution of advance care directives can be useful (COR 2a, LOE C-LD)
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF, execution of advance care directives can be useful to improve documentation of treatment preferences, delivery of patient-centered care, and dying in preferred place.

logic_node.action: Discuss option for discontinuation of life-extending therapies through the continuum of care
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF being considered for, or treated with, life-extending therapies, the option for discontinuation should be anticipated and discussed through the continuum of care, including at the time of initiation, and reassessed with changing medical conditions and shifting goals of care. (COR 1, LOE C-LD)

logic_node.action: Formal palliative care referral for patients with Stage D HF or refractory symptoms
logic_node.action_detail: For patients with HF, particularly stage D HF patients, referral to a formal palliative care specialist can be useful for symptom management and shared decision-making. (COR 2a, LOE B-R)

logic_node.action: Timely referral to hospice (COR 2a, LOE C-LD)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with advanced HF with expected survival <6 months, timely referral to hospice can be useful to improve QOL.

logic_node.action: Standardized assessment of patient-reported health status using validated questionnaire (COR 2a, LOE C-LD)
logic_node.action_detail: In patients with HF, standardized assessment of patient-reported health status using a validated questionnaire can be useful to provide incremental information for patient functional status, symptom burden, and prognosis.
